Litigation funding company Burford Capital's share price surged over 9% today, benefiting from a ruling that Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing Taptic Engine patents. Details are as follows.

Apple ruling boosts litigation funder's valuation

Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple's Taptic Engine infringed two patents held by California company Taction Technology.

Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 alongside the first Apple Watch, and the technology later extended to other products including the iPhone, providing haptic feedback for notifications, interactions and other system events.

When Taction filed its patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, it alleged that Apple directly and indirectly infringed its two patents through Taptic Engines used in multiple iPhone and Apple Watch models.

Following Friday's ruling, Taction said the jury had "upheld its patent rights," while Apple stated that it strongly disagreed with the verdict and would appeal.

Earlier today, the Financial Times reported that litigation funder Burford Capital disclosed it held a financial interest in the case, entitling it to $1.4 billion of the $5.7 billion award if it is ultimately paid in full.

After Burford's announcement, its London-listed shares jumped, closing up 9.41% with a market capitalisation of £659.9 million (approximately $875 million).

Bloomberg Law noted that court records show Taction had received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also indicated that Kenosha was identified as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which provided litigation financing in return for a cut of any future settlement proceeds.

In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the $5.7 billion award is paid in full, its $1.4 billion share would be split roughly evenly between its own balance sheet and its investment funds.
